messages:
tayler: Heads-up — prefix-cache hit rate tanked after last runtime/kernel deploy. Rolled forward 2.1.0+flash-attn yesterday and we dropped from ~92% -> ~43% on gpt-small-v2-int8 traffic. p50 stable but token cost and tail latency jittered.

tayler: Quick metrics snapshot: model=gpt-small-v2-int8, runtime=2.1.0+flash, prefix_hit=0.43, qps=12k, warmup_hit=0.12

nikhil: Do we know if the model fingerprint changed at compile time, or if cache keying logic changed? Any differences in how we tag quant/profile flags?

tayler: No explicit model version bump on the customer side — same model artifact. We did change kernel selection heuristics so some shards are now served by the new flash-opt kernels. Also a minor compile path now writes a "compile_id" into model metadata.

sasha: I dug into the compile artifacts — we started emitting a short compile fingerprint and a quant_profile tag. Key thing: compile-time metadata uses qmode="symmetric" and runtime uses qmode="asymmetric" for a few builds (annotated in build.yml). That means the model tag in the key differs across compile vs runtime builds. Also we subtly changed KV layout ordering for one kernel variant.

perf-bot: Perf regression probe results:
- baseline (2.0.x, old-kernel): prefix_hit_rate=0.92
- canary (2.1.0+flash, new-kernel): prefix_hit_rate=0.43
- A/B rollback (same traffic, pinned kernel to old): prefix_hit_rate restored to 0.89
(Collected over 4h windows on identical prompt sample set)

nikhil: That points to cache-key divergence or a serialization mismatch. Our key generation currently is basically:
```
key = sha256(model_name + '|' + quant_profile + '|' + prompt_prefix[:240] + '|' + tokenizer.version)
```
If quant_profile or tokenizer.version differ across compile/runtime or kernels, we will get misses.

sasha: Additionally, we discovered that some frontends trim trailing whitespace in one path but not another — prompt canonicalization inconsistency. Combined with different quant metadata this explains the hit oscillation.

tayler: Proposed immediate mitigations: canonicalize prompt (normalize whitespace, NFKC), decouple transient compile_id from the stable cache key (use deterministic model fingerprint based on weights hash + model architecture + quant deterministic flags), and add a compatibility map for quant_profile aliases (sym <-> asym) so we treat them equivalently for keys. Also add a sticky mapping so existing cache entries can be looked up by alternate key variants for 48h after a kernel change.

sasha: I'll open a PR to the key canonicalizer today. I also want a CI check that runs a small set of canonicalization tests across kernel flags during compile to catch this earlier.

infra-bot: Created INF-3124: "prefix-cache: canonicalize keys + compatibility map for quant flags". Scheduling a 10% canary tonight at 22:00 UTC after the patch.

tayler: Plan: patch -> canary 10% (2h) -> monitor prefix_hit, warmup_hit, p99 token latency -> roll forward if prefix_hit > 0.8. Owners: sasha (keyfix PR), nikhil (kernel mapping and rollback hooks), tayler (monitoring/alerts).

perf-bot: One more note from profiling: the new kernel's batching heuristic increased average per-batch prefix diversity (we favor kernels with higher throughput even when prefix lengths vary). That reduced reuse in a batch and caused more KV eviction pressure on the warmup window. Suggest lowering batch target thresholds for prefix-heavy workloads or biasing kernel selection when prefix-cache warmup is in progress.

nikhil: Agreed. I'll run a synthetic warmup ramp (6h) on canary to prepopulate the hot prefixes and track evictions. If warmup + keyfix restores hit_rate we can promote.

tayler: Thanks — will post updates here. :thumbsup: (reacts with :eyes:)
